# ScoreMidiLoader { #timetoalign.loader.midi.score.ScoreMidiLoader }

```python
loader.midi.score.ScoreMidiLoader(
    part_voice_assign_mode=0,
    quantization_unit=None,
    estimate_voice_info=False,
    estimate_key=False,
    assign_note_ids=True,
    parser='partitura',
    unit=None,
    number_type=None,
    **kwargs,
)
```

Load score MIDI files using partitura or a mido fast path.

This loader uses partitura's sophisticated MIDI parsing to extract structural
information like voices, parts, and specific pitches (optional). It is ideal
for quantized MIDI files representing scores.

The default partitura parser emits :class:`ScoreMidiEventData`, the wider
schema containing ``voice``, ``staff``, and ``part_id``. ``parser="mido"``
parses only MIDI messages and emits the base :class:`MidiEventData` schema;
it is appropriate when structural score information is not required.
Both parsers write each note's ``velocity`` as its note-on message states
it; partitura's score parse keeps none, so the default path reads the
velocities from the same file and joins them to partitura's notes by
partitura's note number, checking onset, pitch and duration. A note that
cannot be joined that way (a partitura release numbering its notes
otherwise) keeps an empty velocity, and one ``UserWarning`` per file names
the first such note; ``parser="mido"`` reads every velocity.

A MIDI file states no note IDs, so every event ID is minted by the
loader's minter (``note_…``), whichever parser reads the file.
